title: Dharmarajika Stupa
geometryBasis: The named OpenStreetMap site encloses the whole heritage complex. The Pakistan Department of Archaeology and Museums provides the geographic point used to place the stupa. Printed scale and compass establish the terrace and adjacent chapel layout.
sectionBasis: Plates IV and IX of the 1918 guide establish the ground plan and rough damaged limestone drum and immediate masonry. The Taxila Museum specifies the 131 ft drum diameter and 45 ft surviving height.
limitations: The government point places the monument. Its exact surveyed center is uncertain at the imagery and map resolution.
Chapel heights and masonry fracture detail are estimates. The representation depicts the exposed ruins and does not reconstruct lost upper architecture.
The 30 m elevation grid includes monument surface returns. Terrain resolution cannot locate individual masonry courses.
